findings.text: The guard-fires paragraph states that removing the after_suite arm from the delivered fixture returns the row to observe, but no log records that run: the base receipt it points at (base_run_file-1795066204386889164.log) ran the pre-fix pointer, which carried neither a worktree nor a gate arm, so it does not isolate the arm the sentence removes, and the manifest's negative_control_note repeats the claim in prose only. The behaviour is plausible from the predicate, but the paragraph reports a measurement the run did not keep.

after_suite declares revision=09765d47074dc931c6bd1f2ed9386a7f55e86688 while the log_path it cites (after_suite-1795066368223168843.log) heads '# revision: 4816d1987a7723d0b6cfcf4eec43cbd60fa41656'; the arm actually run at the declared head is after_suite-1795067006984452894.log (58 passed, EXIT=0), so the pair is green but the record pairs a revision with a log taken at another one.

The landing line says the named file passes 'in full at head 09765d4707' 'as an all_debug job', but every run of tests/test_crew_scoring_state.py in the run directory heads '# revision: 4816d1987a7723d0b6cfcf4eec43cbd60fa41656' (scoped-gate-1795066500413230275.log, head_run_file-1795066255231015970.log) and no log or scheduler sidecar names the partition, a job id or SLURM_JOB_ID - the .scheduler sidecars beside the arms are empty - so both clauses of the measure rest on prose rather than on a recorded fact.
